claims: The Artemis II mission successfully splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California, on April 10, 2026, at 8:07 p.m. EDT.
The Artemis II mission's four-astronaut crew safely returned after a 10-day trip around the Moon.
The Artemis II mission is the first crewed lunar mission since 1972.
The goal of the Artemis II mission was to test the Orion spacecraft's life support systems.
The goal of the Artemis II mission was to verify safety for future lunar landings.
The Orion capsule separated from its service module during the Artemis II splashdown and recovery.
The Orion capsule descended using parachutes during the Artemis II splashdown and recovery.
Recovery teams from the USS John P. Murtha assisted the Artemis II crew.
The crew of the Artemis II mission consisted of Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
The Artemis III mission is currently scheduled to land humans back on the surface of the Moon.
